record.paper_title: Open problems in Gaussian fluid queueing theory
record.original_question: For the Gaussian fluid queue above, assume that the variance function σ_X^2(t) is regularly varying at infinity with index α_∞ in [1,2). Determine whether the correlation function ρ(t)=Corr(Q(t),Q(0)) has the following asymptotic behavior as t→∞: if α_∞=1, then log ρ(t)/t converges to −γ_1 for some constant γ_1 in (0,∞); if α_∞ is in (1,2), then ρ(t) divided by σ_X^2(t)/t^2 converges to γ_{α_∞} for some constant γ_{α_∞} in (0,∞).

evidence.quote: Both classes of inputs possess the property that σ2_X(t) is regularly varying at ∞ with index α∞ ∈ [1, 2).

Conjecture 2.1 (i) If α∞ = 1, then for some constant γ1 ∈ (0,∞), as t → ∞, lim t→∞ log ρ(t) / t = −γ1. (ii) If α∞ ∈ (1, 2), then for some constant γα∞ ∈ (0,∞), as t → ∞, lim t→∞ ρ(t) / (σ2_X(t)/t2) = γα∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{X(t):t\ge 0\}$ be a centered Gaussian process with stationary increments, $X(0)=0$, and continuous sample paths. Denote its variance function by $\sigma_X^2(t)=\mathrm{Var}(X(t))$, and assume there exists a drift $c>0$ such that the stationary workload (Gaussian fluid queue content)
$$Q(t)=\sup_{s\le t}\bigl(X(t)-X(s)-c(t-s)\bigr)$$
is well defined and has finite variance, with $Q$ a stationary process. Define the workload correlation function
$$\rho(t)=\mathrm{Corr}(Q(t),Q(0)),\qquad t\ge 0.$$
Suppose that $\sigma_X^2(t)$ is regularly varying at infinity with index $\alpha_\infty\in[1,2)$ (that is, for every $\lambda>0$, $\sigma_X^2(\lambda t)/\sigma_X^2(t)\to\lambda^{\alpha_\infty}$ as $t\to\infty$).

Decide whether the following two statements hold:

(i) If $\alpha_\infty=1$, then there exists a constant $\gamma_1\in(0,\infty)$ such that
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\log\rho(t)}{t}=-\gamma_1.$$

(ii) If $\alpha_\infty\in(1,2)$, then there exists a constant $\gamma_{\alpha_\infty}\in(0,\infty)$ such that
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\rho(t)}{\sigma_X^2(t)/t^2}=\gamma_{\alpha_\infty}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. It is posed as a conjecture in the work introducing it, and subsequent literature on correlation structures of Gaussian and Lévy-driven queues (e.g., transient asymptotics and correlation studies of Lévy-driven queues) does not report a proof of either case (i) or (ii) for general regularly varying Gaussian inputs.
